us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic headlines from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Idaho fast-food shooting leaves 3 dead and 7 injured
bullets: A shooting began Saturday at an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho.
Officials said three people were killed and seven others were injured, some critically.
Police found the suspected gunman dead nearby and said the threat to the community was over.

articles.title: FBI probes cyberattacks on Michigan and Minnesota water systems
bullets: Michigan reported cyberattacks on nine water systems after similar reports in Minnesota.
Minnesota officials said more than 30 water systems were targeted earlier in the week.
Authorities said systems were operating safely while the source of the attacks is investigated.

articles.title: Trump criticizes Pirro after Reflecting Pool vandalism case is dropped
bullets: Jeanine Pirro’s office moved to drop charges against former Olympian David Hearn.
Prosecutors said newly reviewed documents pointed to construction problems, not vandalism.
Trump said he disagreed with Pirro and continued to claim vandals caused major damage.

articles.title: Trump settlement-fund threat complicates attorney general talks
bullets: Trump threatened to pursue an “anti-weaponization” settlement fund.
The move added uncertainty to talks over an attorney general nomination.
Senate Republicans were weighing how the proposal could affect confirmation dynamics.

articles.title: Western US heat wave brings record temperatures and wildfire risk
bullets: A heat dome pushed temperatures near record highs across parts of the West.
Forecasters warned the heat could worsen wildfire conditions in dry or already burning areas.
Officials urged residents to use cooling centers and avoid prolonged outdoor exposure.

articles.title: Trump says Mideast allies outlined a deal to end Iran war
bullets: Trump said regional allies had reached the outlines of a deal to end the Iran war.
He said the US would stop new strikes if the parameters hold.
The announcement followed diplomatic calls with Middle East leaders.

articles.title: Iceland seizes Paul Watson Foundation anti-whaling ship
bullets: Icelandic coast guard authorities seized the Paul Watson Foundation ship Bandero.
The vessel’s 21 crew members were detained after the anti-whaling operation.
The seizure escalated tensions around Iceland’s whaling activities.

articles.title: UEFA says it has no confidence in FIFA’s Infantino
bullets: UEFA criticized FIFA President Gianni Infantino after a failed World Cup private-equity plan.
European football officials vowed accountability over the proposal.
The dispute adds to governance tensions between UEFA and FIFA.

articles.title: WestJet flight attendants strike in Canada pay dispute
bullets: WestJet flight attendants went on strike amid a dispute over pay.
The strike affected travelers during a busy summer travel period.
The airline and union remained at odds over compensation and work terms.

articles.title: Moroccan migrants seek entry into Spain’s Ceuta enclave
bullets: Young Moroccans attempted to cross into Spanish territory at Ceuta.
Some said they were seeking work and better opportunities in Europe.
The crossings highlighted continuing migration pressure at Spain’s North African border.

articles.title: FIR names foreign handlers of Bengal terror suspect
bullets: West Bengal Police named several foreign handlers in the FIR against Hamim Mondal.
Authorities said Mondal was arrested in Purba Bardhaman by the state Special Task Force.
The FIR alleges contacts through social media and WhatsApp numbers linked to Pakistan and other countries.

articles.title: Nathu La Pass trade reopens after six-year gap
bullets: Trade through the Nathu La Pass reopened after a six-year suspension.
Traders welcomed the move and said they hoped cross-border commerce would revive.
The route is part of the historic Silk Route linking Sikkim with Tibet.

articles.title: Pune family of three dies amid financial distress
bullets: Police said a man, his wife and daughter died in Pune over alleged financial distress.
Officials reported recovery of sodium nitrate and a suicide note.
The case involved a family with professional and education-sector backgrounds.

articles.title: IIT Guwahati student drowns in Brahmaputra
bullets: Two IIT Guwahati students reportedly slipped into the Brahmaputra River outside campus.
One student drowned and another was rescued with injuries.
Police said the students had gone to spend time by the riverside.

articles.title: PM Modi launches anti-drugs youth campaign
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign.
He said drugs may give a brief high but damage an entire life.
The campaign is aimed at eliminating substance abuse among young people.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Market movers and trading themes investors are watching

articles.title: Dow rises 300 points as S&P 500 hits a record
bullets: US equities rallied in a broad risk-on session.
CNBC reported the S&P 500 reached a new record during the advance.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained about 300 points in the move.

articles.title: Small caps rally while Magnificent 7 stocks rotate lower
bullets: Small-cap stocks outperformed in a market-rotation trade.
Large technology leaders lagged as investors shifted exposure.
The move suggested broader participation beyond mega-cap tech names.

articles.title: Paramount Skydance, Cava, Capri and SailPoint lead midday movers
bullets: CNBC listed Paramount Skydance, Cava, Capri and SailPoint among major midday movers.
The group reflected a mix of media, restaurant, retail and software stock action.
Traders focused on company-specific news alongside broader market gains.

articles.title: Crypto exchange Bullish surges in NYSE debut
bullets: Bullish shares more than doubled after the company’s NYSE debut.
The IPO was priced above its expected range, according to CNBC-linked market coverage.
The move signaled strong investor appetite for crypto-related public listings.

articles.title: CoreWeave drops after earnings as analysts reassess AI demand
bullets: Nvidia-backed CoreWeave fell sharply after its earnings report.
Analysts debated whether weakness would be bought given AI infrastructure demand.
The stock remained a closely watched AI data-center and cloud-computing name.

articles.title: Trump stands to profit by selling fast access to social media posts
bullets: AP reported Trump could profit from selling rapid access to his Truth Social posts.
The service could give traders faster visibility into policy-sensitive announcements.
The report raised questions about market access and presidential communications.

articles.title: US economy grows sluggishly as mortgage rates hit yearly high
bullets: AP’s economy roundup said US growth remained sluggish.
Mortgage rates reached their highest level in a year.
The report covered inflation, unemployment, the Fed and economic effects of the Iran conflict.

articles.title: WestJet strike disrupts airline operations
bullets: WestJet flight attendants struck over pay and working conditions.
The labor action created disruption for Canada’s travel market.
The dispute added to pressure on airlines during peak summer demand.

articles.title: American malls split between decline and reinvention
bullets: AP reported that many US malls are struggling while others are thriving.
Successful malls are shifting toward mixed-use, entertainment and dining experiences.
The story reflects changing consumer behavior and retail real-estate pressures.

articles.title: Trump administration ends Medicare drug subsidy program
bullets: The administration is ending a Medicare drug subsidy program created under Biden.
The change could affect prescription drug costs for some beneficiaries.
Insurers and consumers are assessing the financial impact.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s xAI challenges Minnesota deepfake law
bullets: xAI sued Minnesota over its law banning AI “nudification” technology.
The law targets nonconsensual AI-generated sexual images.
The case tests state regulation of emerging generative-AI tools.

articles.title: Instagram and YouTube found liable in social media addiction trial
bullets: A jury found Instagram and YouTube liable in a landmark social media addiction case.
The verdict focused on claims tied to youth use and platform design.
The case could shape future litigation against major social media companies.

articles.title: AP explains why wet phones should not be put in rice
bullets: AP’s tech tip advised against using rice to dry a wet smartphone.
The guidance recommended safer drying steps instead of common household myths.
The story focused on consumer-device care and damage prevention.

articles.title: Alliance University launches Quantum AI school
bullets: Alliance University launched a Quantum AI School with an 8-qubit computing centre.
The new hub combines quantum computing, AI, robotics and technology entrepreneurship.
The campus is positioned as an interdisciplinary technology education initiative.

articles.title: Indian community in China flags anti-India social media content
bullets: Indian diaspora members in China raised concerns at an embassy Open House.
They flagged visa issues and abusive anti-India content on social media.
The issue links online platforms with diaspora safety and diplomatic engagement.
